With 2 decisions left, the remaining motion I can buy (10-25 mm per plain move_to) is far short of the ~12 cm transport plus release still needed, so the task cannot be completed in budget.", "hindsight": "Rig facts I had to learn the hard way. (1) move_to executes very few control steps unless the gripper changes: step count is about ceil(largest per-dimension delta / 0.037), so a 3-10 cm arm command buys only 2-5 steps and the arm advances only 10-25 mm per call, while a full gripper stroke takes ~80 steps (0.0123 per step). Pairing a long travel with a gripper toggle is therefore the only way to cover >5 cm in one call, and a 1.57 rad yaw target buys only ~5 steps and dragged the hand +4 cm in y as a side effect. (2) The reported eef z is at or just above the fingertip line: the pad span extends UPWARD from the reported point. A ~5 cm block on the 0.80 m table has its top at ~0.85, so closing at z 0.851 or 0.892 shuts the jaws in empty air; a real grasp needs the eef commanded to about 0.82-0.83, which is inside the z bound of 0.80. (3) Do not combine the final descent with the close: the jaws ramp shut over 80 steps while the arm sinks only ~0.4 mm/step, so the pad tops catch the block edge and flick it out of the jaw line. Descend with the jaws open, then close with no other dimension moving. (4) Measured gripper saturates: ~0.99 open, ~0.016 fully shut, so an intermediate reading is the only positive evidence of holding something. (5) Camera axes: front and side are orthogonal fixed views; the side view shows the arm base at the right and separates objects along the reach axis, the wrist camera is tilted forward so image-up is roughly the reach direction, and the wrist view cannot tell whether the block is between the pads or simply below them - only the side view resolves that. (6) Budget: 20 decisions with 10-25 mm per plain call means at most ~0.3 m of total arm travel, so plan the approach from a pose already near the block instead of spending calls on triangulation probes."}
